chapter: Learning the trombone and jam sessions
title: How he got the name Trummy
summary: His parents called him James O.; Booker Coleman, who could not remember names, called him Trummy; he corrects Chilton and discusses mislabeled Lunceford records.

story.theme_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band monikers
story.community_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band names

blocks.x: What were your parents names?
My mother's name was Annie, and my father's name was the same as mine. But they didn't call me junior. (Laughter)
What did they call you?

He used to call me James. You know, most of them down there call me that. James O. My father called me James O. My mother did. Most of my friends called me James or Jim, you know, Jimmy. But I didn't get that name "Trummy" until later years around Washington. And this guy Booker Coleman named me that.

But how we got that name is he couldn't remember names. So, he called the bass player Bassie, and he called the drummer Drumski, and he called me Trummy. And just my name just stuck. That Trummy just stuck. But he'd call everybody, you know, Trumpski -- the trumpet player -- that's because he couldn't remember names. It wasn't because he was trying to give me any name. But that name just stuck on me, you know.
But in Chilton's book he says Tommy Miles gave you that name.
No.
It wasn't Tommy Miles?
No.
Booker Coleman.
Booker Coleman gave me that name. He was wrong.
And it stuck for good because I notice on --
Before I went with Tommy. Booker --
So, you already had it when --
Yeah, Booker named me that.
But I notice on some of the Lunceford record labels it has "Bobo" by Jimmy Young.

No, they made a mistake. They put Johnny Young on one. The first, the very first record I made of "Margie". The guy They asked me, you know, being from the South I don't guess you talk very clearly. So, he asked me my name. I said Trummy Young. So, maybe Trummy sounded like Johnny to him, you know, because I remember the original, the first record I made of "Margie" with Lunceford it had Johnny Young on it.
Well, I -- I don't think I have that one but I have some that say -- you look at the trombones and it has James Young on trombone, but --
Yeah.
-- there's a vocal by Jimmy Young.
Yeah, I guess so. I guess --
Did they ever call you Jimmy?

No, not since I've been -- not since I've played professionally. Everybody called me Trummy. In fact, a lot of them didn't know my name was James. Lot of people -- and they don't even know it today, a lot of people don't, you know. Because that name, it's been on me so long. Because I've had people say how did you ever get a name like that, and then
when I explain to them it's from the trombone, they say oh, we never thought of that, you know. Strange isn't it, you know. They say we never thought of that, you know.
